correctness.rationale: The graph is the twenty-vertex bipartite Kneser H(5,2), ten two-subsets on each shore with adjacency on disjointness. Ordinary open-neighborhood locating-domination is imposed only on vertices outside the chosen code. For any seven-vertex code, the 10-b right-side unchosen signatures have to be distinct nonzero subsets of a left a-set; this and its symmetric counterpart force (a,b)=(3,4) up to shore swapping. Six signatures on three selected left edges must use exactly nine available incidences: three singleton and three doubleton signatures. The three left edges must be mutually intersecting. Triangle forces a forbidden triple signature from the complementary right edge; a three-edge star forces the right code to be the four star edges and leaves the fourth left star edge undominated. Thus no seven-code exists and monotonicity eliminates smaller codes; five explicit double-star eight-codes show sharpness. Independently enumerated all C(20,8)=125970 eight-masks by directly generating open signatures from the actual H(5,2) graph: exactly 1475 valid, distributed 300/875/300 for left weights 3/4/5. Independently generated the S5 permutations plus side exchange, verifying the supplied thirteen representatives have disjoint orbits covering all 1475 with listed sizes. The distance-two graph on either shore is L(K5), whose five size-four maximal star cliques recover S5 and show the automorphism group has order 240. The source verify.py also implements the complete 2^20 all-code cross-check, but its success log is not substituted for this proof or the independent eight-mask census.
